Its Lean proof would have to re-formalize the area formula and dominated convergence (about 650 Lean lines in the accepted c1_piece_tangent subtree).

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit d626082a69a0). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. It is already a resolved dependency of this node. Used by this node's assembly (parent step 1: Q = range Dψ(v₀)). The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: Continuity of the inverse of a proper injective chart (Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every v ∈ V and ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Distances are Euclidean. No openness of V or W is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ W → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → ∀ v ∈ V, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε

Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4, Definition (4.1) and the remark before (4.2) (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 849–862). There Simon notes that "the above definition ensures the local representation is a homeomorphism of V onto the image M ∩ W"; the properness condition of (4.1) is what makes this work. This child is step 2 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space), restricted to the hypotheses that step actually uses. Openness of V and W is not needed. Distances are Euclidean.
Fix v ∈ V and ε > 0, and write q := ψ(v).
1. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no δ > 0 has the stated property. Then for every j ∈ ℕ the number δ = 1/(j+1) > 0 fails. So there is v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε.
2. We have 0 ≤ |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and 1/(j+1) → 0. By squeezing, ψ(v_j) → q as j → ∞.
3. Let K := {q} ∪ {ψ(v_j) : j ∈ ℕ}. K is compact because it is the range of a convergent sequence together with its limit. Indeed, given an open cover of K, one member contains q, and by step 2 it contains ψ(v_j) for all j ≥ j₀. Finitely many further members cover ψ(v_0), …, ψ(v_{j₀−1}).
4. K ⊆ W. For each j, v_j ∈ V, so ψ(v_j) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W. Also v ∈ V, so q = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W.
5. By the properness hypothesis applied to the compact set K ⊆ W, the set C := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact. Every v_j lies in C, because v_j ∈ V and ψ(v_j) ∈ K. C is a compact subset of the metric space ℝ^d, hence sequentially compact. So there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a point v* ∈ C with v_{φ(i)} → v* as i → ∞. In particular v* ∈ V.
6. Now v* ∈ V, every v_{φ(i)} lies in V, and v_{φ(i)} → v*. Since ψ is continuous on V, it is continuous at v* relative to V, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → ψ(v*). On the other hand, (ψ(v_{φ(i)}))_i is a subsequence of (ψ(v_j))_j, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → q by step 2. Limits in ℝ^P are unique, hence ψ(v*) = q = ψ(v).
7. Both v* and v lie in V, and ψ is injective on V, so v* = v. Thus v_{φ(i)} → v. Hence |v_{φ(i)} − v| < ε for some i. This contradicts step 1, which gives |v_j − v| ≥ ε for every j, in particular for j = φ(i).
8. So the assumption in step 1 is false. There is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Since v ∈ V and ε > 0 were arbitrary, the statement is proved.
proof_key_steps: Negating the claim gives v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε, so ψ(v_j) → ψ(v).
K = {ψ(v)} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} is compact and lies in W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact and contains every v_j.
A subsequence v_{φ(i)} converges to some v* ∈ V. Continuity of ψ on V and uniqueness of limits give ψ(v*) = ψ(v).
Injectivity on V gives v* = v, which contradicts |v_{φ(i)} − v| ≥ ε.

subproblems.title: Lower Lipschitz bound for a C¹ map near a point where its derivative is injective
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be a C¹ map and let x ∈ ℝ^n be a point at which the derivative DG(x) : ℝ^n → ℝ^P is injective. Then there are δ > 0 and μ > 0 such that μ|a − b| ≤ |G(a) − G(b)| for all a, b in the open ball B_δ(x). Here ℝ^k = Euclid k carries the Euclidean norm |·|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (x : Euclid n), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → Injective (fderiv ℝ G x) → ∃ δ μ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ 0 < μ ∧ ∀ a ∈ ball x δ, ∀ b ∈ ball x δ, μ * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖G a - G b‖

The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source. Step 5 of the parent proof of Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–66; the 'only if' part is lines 39–65).
- The printed proof says: if the Jacobian of G_{ij} is non-zero at x, then for some ρ > 0 the set G_{ij}(B_ρ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}, with G_{ij} as a local representation. (Erratum: the book prints ℝ^n.)
- The parent proof records the quantitative content of this inverse-function argument as a lower Lipschitz bound on a ball. That bound is the present statement, for a single C¹ map G.
- A non-zero Jacobian J_G(x) = √det(DG(x)* DG(x)) means exactly that DG(x) is injective.
Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖A‖ the operator norm of a linear map A, and B_δ(x) the open ball.

1. (Coercivity of L.) Put L := DG(x), an injective linear map ℝ^n → ℝ^P.
- Since ℝ^n is finite-dimensional, L is a linear isomorphism of ℝ^n onto the subspace L(ℝ^n). Its inverse L(ℝ^n) → ℝ^n is linear on a finite-dimensional normed space, hence bounded.
- So there is N > 0 with |v| ≤ N|Lv| for every v ∈ ℝ^n. (Equivalently: if n ≥ 1, v ↦ |Lv| is continuous and positive on the compact unit sphere, so it has a positive minimum. If n = 0, every v is 0 and any N > 0 works.)
- Put μ := 1/(2N) > 0. Then |Lv| ≥ |v|/N = 2μ|v| for all v ∈ ℝ^n.
2. (Continuity of DG at x.) G is C¹, so y ↦ DG(y) is continuous from ℝ^n into the linear maps ℝ^n → ℝ^P with the operator norm, in particular at x. Choose δ > 0 with ‖DG(y) − L‖ ≤ μ for all y ∈ B_δ(x).
3. (Mean value inequality.) Let φ(y) := G(y) − L(y).
- Since L is linear, φ is differentiable at every y with Dφ(y) = DG(y) − L. So ‖Dφ(y)‖ ≤ μ for y ∈ B_δ(x).
- The ball B_δ(x) is convex, so the mean value inequality gives |φ(a) − φ(b)| ≤ μ|a − b| for all a, b ∈ B_δ(x).
- Since L is linear, φ(a) − φ(b) = G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b). Hence |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ μ|a − b|.
4. (Conclusion.) Let a, b ∈ B_δ(x). By the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3,
 |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ |L(a − b)| − |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≥ 2μ|a − b| − μ|a − b| = μ|a − b|.
So δ > 0 and μ > 0 have the required property. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). No extra import is needed.
- Step 1: apply LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz to (fderiv ℝ G x : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P). This gives N > 0 with AntilipschitzWith N. ZeroHomClass.bound_of_antilipschitz then gives ‖v‖ ≤ N * ‖L v‖.
- Steps 2–3 together say that G approximates L with constant μ near x, which is strict differentiability:
  - hG.contDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt (by norm_num) : HasStrictFDerivAt G (fderiv ℝ G x) x.
  - HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds with c := ⟨μ, hμ.le⟩ gives s ∈ 𝓝 x with ApproximatesLinearOn G L s c. This means ‖G a - G b - L (a - b)‖ ≤ μ * ‖a - b‖ for a, b ∈ s; apply it as happrox a ha b hb.
  - Metric.mem_nhds_iff gives δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ s.
  - Alternatively, use Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le directly for step 3.
- Step 4: norm_sub_le, then nlinarith.
proof_key_steps: L := DG(x) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝ^n, so there is N > 0 with |v| ≤ N|Lv|. Put μ := 1/(2N), so |Lv| ≥ 2μ|v| for all v.
Since G is C¹, DG is continuous at x. This gives δ > 0 with ‖DG(y) − L‖ ≤ μ on B_δ(x); equivalently, use strict differentiability at x.
The mean value inequality for G − L on the convex ball gives |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ μ|a − b| for a, b ∈ B_δ(x).
By the triangle inequality, |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ 2μ|a − b| − μ|a − b| = μ|a − b| on B_δ(x).

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a C¹ piece with a lower Lipschitz bound (proof of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 '⇒')
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P a C¹ map, c ∈ ℝ^n, r ∈ ℝ and m > 0 with m|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b in the open ball B := B_r(c). Then for every z ∈ B, the set N := g(B) has approximate tangent space T := Dg(z)(ℝ^n) = range(fderiv ℝ g z) at g(z) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (g z) T): dim T = n, and ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(N)} f dH^n → ∫_T f dH^n as s ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Here η_{w,s}(y) = s^{-1}(y − w) and H^n = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (c : Euclid n) (r m : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ ball c r, ∀ b ∈ ball c r, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖g a - g b‖) → ∀ z ∈ ball c r, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g '' ball c r) (g z) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.codim1_rdo_c1_piece_approxTangent of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1.c1_piece_tangent-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 9ff76906722d). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Its candidate commit also carries its accepted prerequisites codim1_rdo_c1pt_fderiv_lower_bound, codim1_rdo_c1pt_rescaled_area_formula, codim1_rdo_c1pt_linear_range_integral and codim1_rdo_c1pt_rescaled_integral_tendsto, adds no imports (it proves the area formula in place, so the import mentioned in the implementation note of the verbatim proof below was not needed), and its declaration depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Used by the new child chart_ball_tangent (its proof is parent steps 4–9: rescaled area formula, integrable bound, pointwise limit, dominated convergence, linear area formula). The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source. Step 3 of the parent proof. It supplies the details of Simon's assertion in the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 113–125): 'since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dH^n = ∫_{T_xN_j} f dH^n'. The computation uses the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative (Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.2)); in SimonGMT this is Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, a Bochner-integral identity valid for every integrand.
Notation:
- H^n = μHE[n], which equals Lebesgue measure L^n on ℝ^n.
- J(a) := J_g(a) = √det(Dg(a)*Dg(a)), the metric Jacobian of g at a ∈ ℝ^n (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt g a = normDet(Dg(a))).
- For a linear map L, J_L := √det(L*L).
- w := g(z), and η_{w,s}(y) = s^{-1}(y − w) (blowUpMap).

1. (Injective derivatives; dim T = n.) Let a ∈ B and v ∈ ℝ^n. Since B is open, a + tv ∈ B for small t > 0, and then mt|v| ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|. Dividing by t and letting t ↓ 0 gives m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v|. So Dg(a) is injective for every a ∈ B. In particular L := Dg(z) is injective, and T = L(ℝ^n) has dimension n.

2. (Continuity of J.) Dg is continuous, and J(a)² is the determinant of the Gram matrix (⟨Dg(a)e_i, Dg(a)e_j⟩)_{i,j}, a polynomial in the entries of Dg(a). So a ↦ J(a) = √(J(a)²) is continuous. (SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet gives continuity of L ↦ normDet L directly.)

3. (Area formula for the blow-ups.) Fix s > 0 and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Let B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}, an open (hence Borel) set, and φ_s(b) := s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − w).
- φ_s(B_s) = η_{w,s}(N): each a ∈ B is a = z + sb with b = (a − z)/s ∈ B_s, and η_{w,s}(g(a)) = s^{-1}(g(a) − w).
- φ_s is differentiable with Dφ_s(b) = Dg(z + sb) by the chain rule; this is injective for b ∈ B_s by step 1.
- φ_s is injective on B_s: |φ_s(b) − φ_s(b')| = s^{-1}|g(z + sb) − g(z + sb')| ≥ m|b − b'|.
Hence J_{φ_s}(b) = J(z + sb), and the area formula gives
 I(s) := ∫_{η_{w,s}(N)} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) dL^n(b).

4. (Localisation.) Choose R > 0 with f = 0 outside closedBall(0, R), which is possible since f has compact support. Choose ρ₀ > 0 with closedBall(z, ρ₀) ⊆ B, possible since B is open. Let K := closedBall(0, R/m) ⊆ ℝ^n and s₀ := mρ₀/R > 0. For 0 < s ≤ s₀:
(a) K ⊆ B_s: if |b| ≤ R/m then |sb| ≤ ρ₀, so z + sb ∈ B.
(b) If b ∈ B_s ∖ K, then |φ_s(b)| = s^{-1}|g(z + sb) − g(z)| ≥ m|b| > R, so f(φ_s(b)) = 0.
Hence I(s) = ∫_K J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) dL^n(b) for 0 < s ≤ s₀.

5. (Pointwise limit.) Fix b ∈ K and let s ↓ 0.
- φ_s(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)) → Lb, by differentiability of g at z.
- J(z + sb) → J(z), by step 2.
- f is continuous.
Hence J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) → J(z) f(Lb).

6. (Dominated convergence.) Let Λ := max{J(a) : a ∈ closedBall(z, ρ₀)}, finite as the maximum of a continuous function on a compact set.
- For 0 < s ≤ s₀ and b ∈ K we have z + sb ∈ closedBall(z, ρ₀), so |J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b))| ≤ Λ sup|f|.
- This constant is integrable on K, since L^n(K) < ∞.
- For each s the integrand is continuous in b, hence measurable, and the filter s ↓ 0 is countably generated.
Dominated convergence therefore gives I(s) → ∫_K J(z) f(Lb) dL^n(b).

7. (Identification of the limit.) If |b| > R/m then |Lb| ≥ m|b| > R by step 1, so f(Lb) = 0. Hence ∫_K J(z) f(Lb) db = ∫_{ℝ^n} J(z) f(Lb) db. Now apply the area formula of step 3 to the injective linear map L on ℝ^n. Its derivative is L at every point, so its Jacobian is J_L = J(z) = J_g(z), and L(ℝ^n) = T. This gives ∫_{ℝ^n} J(z) f(Lb) db = ∫_T f dH^n.

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6 and 7, ∫_{η_{w,s}(N)} f dH^n → ∫_T f dH^n as s ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Together with dim T = n (step 1), this shows that T = range Dg(z) is the approximate tangent space of N = g(B_r(c)) at w = g(z) (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4). ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). The area formula needs `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`, which is prebuilt and already used by accepted DAG nodes. Its measure is μHE[finrank ℝ (Euclid n)], with finrank_euclideanSpace_fin and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume. Dominated convergence along 𝓝[>] 0 is Mathlib's tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence.
proof_key_steps: The lower Lipschitz bound gives |Dg(a)v| ≥ m|v| on B. So Dg(a) is injective, and T = Dg(z)(ℝ^n) has dimension n.

With B_s = (B − z)/s and φ_s(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)), φ_s maps B_s injectively onto η_{g(z),s}(N), with Dφ_s(b) = Dg(z + sb). The area formula gives ∫_{η(N)} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J_g(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) db.
For small s the integrand is supported in the fixed ball K = closedBall(0, R/m) ⊆ B_s (lower Lipschitz bound and spt f ⊆ closedBall(0, R)).
Pointwise φ_s(b) → Dg(z)b and J_g(z + sb) → J_g(z), with a uniform bound on K. Dominated convergence gives the limit ∫ J_g(z) f(Dg(z)b) db.
The linear area formula identifies this limit with ∫_T f dH^n.

subproblems.title: A map that is C¹ on an open set agrees near any of its points with a globally C¹ map (bump-function cut-off)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^m be open, let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and let v₀ ∈ V. Then there are a map g : ℝ^m → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^m (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) and a radius ρ > 0 such that the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀). Here ℝ^k = Euclid k with the Euclidean norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → v₀ ∈ V → ∃ (g : Euclid m → Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ ∧ ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ EqOn g ψ (ball v₀ ρ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. A technical step needed to apply the accepted sibling c1_piece_tangent, which is stated for globally C¹ maps, to the chart ψ of parent step 1, which is C¹ only on the open set V. The parent-supplied proof avoids this step by integrating against the indicator 1_{G_r} of the chart domain (parent steps 4–6). The argument is the standard cut-off by a smooth bump function.
Notation: B_s(c) is the open ball, B̄_s(c) the closed ball, |·| the Euclidean norm.
1. (Room in V.) V is open and v₀ ∈ V, so there is ε > 0 with B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V.
2. (Bump function.) Choose a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^m → ℝ with φ(v) = 1 whenever |v − v₀| ≤ ε/4 and φ(v) = 0 whenever |v − v₀| ≥ ε/2. In Mathlib this is a bump function φ : ContDiffBump v₀ with rIn = ε/4 < rOut = ε/2, available on the inner-product space Euclid m. The three properties are ContDiffBump.contDiff, ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall and ContDiffBump.zero_of_le_dist.
3. (Definition.) Put g(v) := φ(v)·ψ(v) for v ∈ ℝ^m, and ρ := ε/4 > 0. Then B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V.
4. (g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀).) If |v − v₀| < ρ = ε/4, then φ(v) = 1 by step 2, so g(v) = ψ(v).
5. (g is C¹ at every point.) A map is C¹ on ℝ^m iff it is C¹ at every point (Mathlib contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Fix v ∈ ℝ^m.
 (a) Case |v − v₀| < ε. Then v ∈ V by step 1, and V, being open, is a neighbourhood of v. ψ is C¹ on V, hence C¹ at v (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). φ is C^∞, in particular C¹ at v. Hence the product g = φ·ψ of a scalar C¹ function and a vector C¹ function is C¹ at v (ContDiffAt.smul).
 (b) Case |v − v₀| ≥ ε. The set O := {w ∈ ℝ^m : |w − v₀| > ε/2} is open, as the preimage of the open ray (ε/2, ∞) under the continuous map w ↦ |w − v₀|. It contains v, because |v − v₀| ≥ ε > ε/2. For w ∈ O we have φ(w) = 0 by step 2, so g(w) = 0. Thus g coincides with the constant map 0 on a neighbourhood of v. The constant map is C¹, so g is C¹ at v (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
 So g is C¹ at every point, i.e. ContDiff ℝ 1 g.
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–5, 0 < ρ, B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V, g is C¹ on ℝ^m, and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V and a C^∞ bump φ equal to 1 on B̄_{ε/4}(v₀) and to 0 outside B_{ε/2}(v₀).
Put g := φ·ψ and ρ := ε/4; then B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V and g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀).
g is C¹ at points of B_ε(v₀) ⊆ V (product of C¹ maps) and at points with |v − v₀| ≥ ε (g = 0 on the open set |w − v₀| > ε/2), hence C¹ on ℝ^m.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent plane of the chart image of a small ball at its centre (parent steps 2 and 4–9)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^m be open, let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and let v₀ ∈ V be a point at which Dψ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ is injective. Then there is ρ > 0 such that the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V and the linear subspace T := range Dψ(v₀) of ℝ^P is the approximate tangent space of the set ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) at the point ψ(v₀) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ(B_ρ(v₀))) (ψ(v₀)) T): dim T = m, and ∫_{η_{ψ(v₀),r}(ψ(B_ρ(v₀)))} f dH^m → ∫_T f dH^m as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^m = μHE[m].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → v₀ ∈ V → Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ v₀) → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V ∧ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ '' ball v₀ ρ) (ψ v₀) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent steps 2 and 4–9, the analytic core of the parent proof, for the chart image of a small ball. It supplies Simon's unproved assertion in the proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 113–126): "since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dH^n = ∫_{T_xN_j} f dH^n".
- Parent steps 4–9 (rescaled area formula, fixed integrable bound, pointwise limit, dominated convergence, linear area formula) are exactly the reviewed and accepted proof of the sibling c1_piece_tangent. That sibling needs a globally C¹ map with a lower Lipschitz bound on a ball.
- The lower Lipschitz bound is parent step 2, (2.1); it is the sibling local_lower_lipschitz.
- The globally C¹ map is supplied by the sibling c1_local_extension.
Notation: A := Dψ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ and T := range A = LinearMap.range A.
1. (Global C¹ extension.) By c1_local_extension, applied to V, ψ and v₀, there are g : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with ContDiff ℝ 1 g and ρ₁ > 0 with B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V and g = ψ on B_{ρ₁}(v₀).
2. (Same value and derivative at v₀.) g(v₀) = ψ(v₀), since v₀ ∈ B_{ρ₁}(v₀). The open ball B_{ρ₁}(v₀) is a neighbourhood of v₀ on which g = ψ. The Fréchet derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the map there (Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so Dg(v₀) = A. In particular Dg(v₀) is injective.
3. (Lower Lipschitz bound; parent step 2.) g is C¹ on ℝ^m and Dg(v₀) is injective. By local_lower_lipschitz, applied to g and v₀, there are δ > 0 and μ > 0 with μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ B_δ(v₀).
4. (Radius.) Put ρ := min(ρ₁, δ) > 0. Then:
- B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V;
- B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_δ(v₀), so μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ B_ρ(v₀);
- v₀ ∈ B_ρ(v₀).
5. (The C¹ piece; parent steps 4–9.) Apply c1_piece_tangent to g, c := v₀, r := ρ, the constant μ > 0 (called m there), and z := v₀ ∈ B_ρ(v₀). It gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (g(B_ρ(v₀))) (g(v₀)) (range Dg(v₀)).
6. (Back to ψ.) g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ B_{ρ₁}(v₀), so g(B_ρ(v₀)) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)): images of one set under two maps that agree on it (Set.EqOn.image_eq). By step 2, g(v₀) = ψ(v₀) and range Dg(v₀) = range A = T. Substituting into step 5 gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (ψ(B_ρ(v₀))) (ψ(v₀)) T.
7. (Conclusion.) Step 4 gives ρ > 0 and B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V. With step 6 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: c1_local_extension gives a globally C¹ map g and ρ₁ > 0 with g = ψ on B_{ρ₁}(v₀) ⊆ V; hence g(v₀) = ψ(v₀) and Dg(v₀) = Dψ(v₀) (equal germs).
local_lower_lipschitz gives δ, μ > 0 with μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| on B_δ(v₀); put ρ := min(ρ₁, δ).
c1_piece_tangent at z = v₀ gives the approximate tangent space range Dg(v₀) of g(B_ρ(v₀)) at g(v₀).
Since g = ψ on B_ρ(v₀), this is the approximate tangent space range Dψ(v₀) of ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) at ψ(v₀).

subproblems.title: Near x = ψ(v₀), the set N ∩ W coincides with the chart image of any open ball around v₀ contained in V (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, N, W, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^m, ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, v₀ ∈ V and ρ > 0. Assume W and W₀ are open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀, ψ(v₀) ∈ W, and the open ball B_ρ(v₀) is contained in V. Then there is δ > 0 with (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (N W W₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid m) (ρ : ℝ), IsOpen W → IsOpen W₀ → ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W₀ ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W₀, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → v₀ ∈ V → ψ v₀ ∈ W → 0 < ρ → ball v₀ ρ ⊆ V → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ N ∩ W ∩ ball (ψ v₀) δ = ψ '' ball v₀ ρ ∩ ball (ψ v₀) δ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 3, (3.1) (localization), together with the inclusion ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ N ∩ W used in the "⊇" half of (4.1). Parent step 3 derives (3.1) from properness and injectivity of the chart by a compactness argument. That argument is the content of the accepted sibling chart_inverse_continuity (ψ^{-1} is continuous at ψ(v₀) along ψ(V); Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2)), which is used here instead.
Notation: x := ψ(v₀); B_s(c) is the open ball; distances are Euclidean.
1. (ψ(V) ⊆ W₀.) ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N ⊆ W₀. Since v₀ ∈ V, x = ψ(v₀) ∈ W₀.
2. (Inverse continuity.) Apply chart_inverse_continuity to V, W₀ (in the role of W there) and ψ, with the point v₀ ∈ V and ε := ρ > 0. Its hypotheses hold: ψ is continuous and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W₀ by step 1, and V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀. It gives δ₁ > 0 such that every v ∈ V with |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| < δ₁ satisfies |v − v₀| < ρ.
3. (Room in W ∩ W₀.) x ∈ W by hypothesis and x ∈ W₀ by step 1. W ∩ W₀ is open, so there is δ₂ > 0 with B_{δ₂}(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀.
4. (Choice of δ.) Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0. Then B_δ(x) ⊆ B_{δ₂}(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀.
5. (⊆.) Let y ∈ N ∩ W with |y − x| < δ. By step 4, y ∈ W₀, so y ∈ W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V): y = ψ(v) for some v ∈ V. Then |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| = |y − x| < δ ≤ δ₁, so |v − v₀| < ρ by step 2, i.e. v ∈ B_ρ(v₀). Hence y ∈ ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x).
6. (⊇.) Let y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B_ρ(v₀) and |y − x| < δ. Since B_ρ(v₀) ⊆ V, y ∈ ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, so y ∈ N. Also y ∈ B_δ(x) ⊆ W by step 4. Hence y ∈ (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(x).
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 6, (N ∩ W) ∩ B_δ(x) = ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ∩ B_δ(x), with δ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_inverse_continuity (ψ(V) ⊆ W₀, properness, injectivity) gives δ₁ > 0: v ∈ V and |ψ(v) − ψ(v₀)| < δ₁ imply |v − v₀| < ρ.
Choose δ₂ > 0 with B_{δ₂}(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W ∩ W₀ and put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂).
⊆: a point of N ∩ W ∩ B_δ(ψ(v₀)) lies in W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V), so it is ψ(v) with v ∈ B_ρ(v₀).
⊇: ψ(B_ρ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N and B_δ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent spaces are local: sets that agree near x have the same approximate tangent spaces at x (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let S, S' ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets (no measurability is assumed), x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and δ > 0 with S ∩ B_δ(x) = S' ∩ B_δ(x), where B_δ(x) is the open ball. If Q is the approximate tangent space of S' at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q: dim Q = n, and ∫_{η_{x,r}(S')} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^n = μHE[n]), then Q is also the approximate tangent space of S at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S S' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → S ∩ ball x δ = S' ∩ ball x δ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 4, (4.1)–(4.2). For f supported in B_R(0) and 0 < r < δ/R, the blow-up η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) meets B_R(0) only in the image of the part of N ∩ W inside B_δ(x). So the integrals of f over η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) and over the blown-up chart piece coincide. Here this is proved for arbitrary sets. The restriction identity of step 3 replaces the parent's use of setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, which needed Borel measurability of η_{x,r}(N ∩ W).
Notation:
- μ := H^n = μHE[n].
- η_r := η_{x,r} (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r), η_r(t) = r^{-1}(t − x).
- For a set T, ∫_T f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against the restricted measure μ⌞T (Lean: ∫ y in T, f y ∂μ). It is defined for every set T.
1. (Dimension.) The first conjunct, dim Q = n, does not involve the set. It holds by the hypothesis on S'.
2. (Support radius.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Its topological support is compact, hence bounded, so there is R₀ with spt f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0). Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. Then spt f ⊆ B_R(0), so f(y) = 0 for every y ∉ B_R(0).
3. (Cut-off of the integral.) For every set T ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_T f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ T} f dμ.
 - f vanishes outside B_R(0), so the integral of f against μ⌞T equals its integral against (μ⌞T)⌞B_R(0) (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, valid for any set and any measure).
 - B_R(0) is open, hence Borel, so (μ⌞T)⌞B_R(0) = μ⌞(B_R(0) ∩ T) (Mathlib Measure.restrict_restrict, which only needs measurability of B_R(0)).
4. (Only the part near x matters.) Let 0 < r < δ/R. For every set T, B_R(0) ∩ η_r(T) = B_R(0) ∩ η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)).
 - ⊇: η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)) ⊆ η_r(T).
 - ⊆: let y = η_r(t) = r^{-1}(t − x) with t ∈ T and |y| < R. Then |t − x| = r|y| < rR < (δ/R)R = δ. So t ∈ T ∩ B_δ(x) and y ∈ η_r(T ∩ B_δ(x)).
5. (Equal blown-up integrals.) Let 0 < r < δ/R. By steps 3 and 4 and the hypothesis S ∩ B_δ(x) = S' ∩ B_δ(x):
 ∫_{η_r(S')} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S')} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S' ∩ B_δ(x))} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S ∩ B_δ(x))} f dμ = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ η_r(S)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ.
6. (Limit.) δ/R > 0, so the interval (0, δ/R) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of r ↓ 0. Hence r ↦ ∫_{η_r(S')} f dμ and r ↦ ∫_{η_r(S)} f dμ agree eventually along r ↓ 0. The first tends to ∫_Q f dμ by the hypothesis on S', so the second does too (Filter.Tendsto.congr').
7. (Conclusion.) f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) was arbitrary. With step 1 this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: The dimension conjunct does not involve the set.
For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) choose R > 0 with spt f ⊆ B_R(0); then ∫_T f dH^n = ∫_{B_R(0) ∩ T} f dH^n for every set T (restriction to the Borel ball).
For 0 < r < δ/R, B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(T) = B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(T ∩ B_δ(x)), so the blown-up integrals over S and S' agree.
They agree eventually along r ↓ 0, so the limit ∫_Q f dH^n transfers from S' to S.
